idiom_name: value-semantic domain classes + to_row/from_row free functions in infra
implementation_notes: The default C++ realization keeps domain classes free of persistence knowledge: private state, invariants in the constructor, and value semantics; the row shape and the conversion live in the infrastructure layer as plain structs plus free functions or a thin Mapper class (to_row/from_row, or to_domain/from_entity). A Mapper class hierarchy is still justified when one mapping is reused across several backends or aggregates, but for a single store free functions plus a repository are clearer and cheaper. No framework provides this in C++, so the structure is hand-written; the compiler does prevent storage types leaking in as long as the domain headers never include the persistence headers.
pitfalls: Slicing and value semantics: passing domain objects by value through the mapper copies state, while storing them polymorphically behind references reintroduces shared mutable graphs the model was meant to encapsulate.
Implicit conversions and aggregate initialization hide field order: a reordered OrderRow silently mis-maps unless the mapper is field-by-field and covered by round-trip tests.
A persistence struct that is not `explicit`-safe (templated constructors, conversion operators) can be constructed from a domain object accidentally, blurring the two models.

variants.name: ODB code generation with non-intrusive pragma headers
variants.idiom_name: ODB compiler + db pragmas moved into a separate header
variants.implementation_notes: ODB generates the conversion code from the class declarations, so no mapping code is written by hand; crucially, the ODB manual documents that pragmas can be moved out of the class into a separate header, keeping the mapping completely non-intrusive and the domain header storage-free. Choose it when a relational database and code generation are acceptable in the build; the classic hand-written mapper stays the better answer when only one or two aggregates are persisted, or when the mapping must apply domain validation on load.
pitfalls: Pragma headers must stay in sync with the domain class; a member rename that is not reflected there breaks the build at the ODB step, not in the model.
The ODB compiler becomes a build dependency and the generated code a review artefact - teams that dislike code generation should stay with the hand-written mapper.
